# sqlalchemy-cubrid

> SQLAlchemy 2.0/2.1 dialect for the CUBRID database: SQL and DDL compilation, type mapping (including native JSON and collection types), schema reflection, CUBRID-specific DML constructs, Alembic migrations, and sync plus async driver support for Python 3.10+ (PEP 561 typed).

sqlalchemy-cubrid lets Python applications use CUBRID with SQLAlchemy Core, the ORM, the asyncio extension, and Alembic. It registers three driver variants: the pure-Python `pycubrid` driver, its asyncio counterpart `pycubrid.aio`, and the legacy `CUBRIDdb` C extension.

Key facts:
- Driver variants (URL scheme, install extra):
  - `cubrid+pycubrid://user:password@host:33000/dbname` — pure-Python pycubrid, recommended for new projects; `pip install "sqlalchemy-cubrid[pycubrid]"` (pycubrid>=1.8.0,<2.0)
  - `cubrid+aiopycubrid://user:password@host:33000/dbname` — async pycubrid for `create_async_engine`; same `[pycubrid]` extra, which also pulls in `sqlalchemy[asyncio]`
  - `cubrid://` (also `cubrid+cubrid://`, `cubrid+cubriddb://`) — legacy CUBRIDdb C extension; build it from cubrid-python v11.3.0.51 or later. The `[cubrid]`/`[cubriddb]` extras are deprecated: they install PyPI `CUBRID-Python` 9.3.x, which is untested, and the dialect emits a `SAWarning` at first connect for a CUBRIDdb older than 11.3
- A bare `pip install sqlalchemy-cubrid` installs no DB-API driver; choose an extra above
- Isolation levels: the three CUBRID MVCC levels `READ COMMITTED` (4, server default), `REPEATABLE READ` (5) and `SERIALIZABLE` (6), plus `AUTOCOMMIT` (driver autocommit). `CURSOR STABILITY` and the two long `... SCHEMA, ... INSTANCES` spellings are accepted only as aliases of levels 4 and 5; the pre-MVCC levels 1–3 are rejected
- Native `JSON` type (CUBRID 10.2+) with `col["key"]` / path indexing compiled to `JSON_EXTRACT`
- No `RETURNING`: get auto-increment keys from `session.flush()` (ORM) or `SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID()` (Core)
- No sequences (`AUTO_INCREMENT` instead); `Boolean` is stored as `SMALLINT`; collection types `SET`, `MULTISET`, `SEQUENCE` instead of arrays
- Collection values: on `cubrid+pycubrid://` / `cubrid+aiopycubrid://` a `list`/`tuple` (and, for `SET`/`MULTISET` only, a `set`/`frozenset`) bound to a `SET`/`MULTISET`/`SEQUENCE` column is sent as a pycubrid typed collection (`pycubrid.types.Set`/`Multiset`/`Sequence`, on pycubrid main and not yet released; released pycubrid 1.8.0 rejects collection parameters). Read them back with `?decode_collections=true` as `frozenset` (SET) or `list` (MULTISET/SEQUENCE). A `SEQUENCE` needs a `list` or `tuple`: a `set`/`frozenset` raises `TypeError` with every pycubrid version. Collections cannot be rendered with `literal_binds`. CUBRIDdb binds every collection as a SET, losing MULTISET duplicates and SEQUENCE order
- Single-schema reflection: only the connection's default schema is recognised; other `schema=` values reflect as missing
- DDL is transactional: `ROLLBACK` undoes it and it never commits earlier DML; only client autocommit (off by default in the dialect) commits it early. Alembic runs a whole upgrade in one transaction (`transactional_ddl = True`); use `transaction_per_migration=True` for long or large-table migrations
- Unquoted identifiers fold to lowercase (not uppercase like the SQL standard)
- CUBRID does not enforce `CHECK` constraints; reflection returns none
- Tested against CUBRID 10.2, 11.0, 11.2 and 11.4

## Docs

- [Quick Start](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/QUICKSTART/): Installation, URL formats, first Core and ORM example
- [Connection Guide](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/CONNECTION/): URL schemes and entry points, pycubrid URL query options (`?connect_timeout=`, `?charset=`, ...), async engine, connection options, autocommit, connection pool tuning
- [Driver Compatibility](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/DRIVER_COMPAT/): CUBRIDdb C-extension versions, exception hierarchy, known driver issues
- [ORM Cookbook](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/ORM_COOKBOOK/): Models, relationships, CRUD, collections, LOBs, CUBRID-specific gotchas
- [DML Extensions](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/DML_EXTENSIONS/): ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, REPLACE INTO, MERGE, GROUP_CONCAT, FOR UPDATE, UPDATE ... LIMIT, index hints, TRUNCATE
- [Type Mapping](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/TYPES/): SQLAlchemy/CUBRID type mapping, collection, LOB and JSON types, boolean handling, reflection
- [Isolation Levels](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/ISOLATION_LEVELS/): The three MVCC levels, accepted aliases, AUTOCOMMIT, engine/connection/execution-option configuration
- [Alembic Migrations](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/ALEMBIC/): Setup, autogenerate, transactional DDL, limitations and batch workarounds

## Reference

- [Feature Support](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/FEATURE_SUPPORT/): Feature comparison with MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite
- [Support Matrix](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/SUPPORT_MATRIX/): Python, SQLAlchemy, CUBRID and driver version compatibility
- [Architecture](https://cubrid-lab.github.io/sqlalchemy-cubrid/ARCHITECTURE/): Dialect internals, compiler pipeline, reflection, module boundaries
- [Source — dialect.py](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/sqlalchemy-cubrid/blob/main/sqlalchemy_cubrid/dialect.py): Main dialect class with reflection, connection handling, isolation levels
- [Source — compiler.py](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/sqlalchemy-cubrid/blob/main/sqlalchemy_cubrid/compiler.py): SQL, DDL and type compilers
- [Source — dml.py](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/sqlalchemy-cubrid/blob/main/sqlalchemy_cubrid/dml.py): `insert()` with ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, `replace()`, `merge()`
- [Source — types.py](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/sqlalchemy-cubrid/blob/main/sqlalchemy_cubrid/types.py): CUBRID type system

## Examples

- [Quick Start — Core](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/sqlalchemy-cubrid/blob/main/README.md#core-connection-level): Connection-level usage with `create_engine` and `text()`
- [Quick Start — ORM](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/sqlalchemy-cubrid/blob/main/README.md#orm-session-level): Declarative ORM model definition and CRUD
- [Quick Start — Async](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/sqlalchemy-cubrid/blob/main/README.md#async): `create_async_engine` with `cubrid+aiopycubrid://`
- [Cookbook — 5-minute SQLAlchemy](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/quickstart/5min-sqlalchemy): SQLAlchemy ORM quickstart against CUBRID in Docker
- [Cookbook — SQLAlchemy fundamentals](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/fundamentals/sqlalchemy): Numbered SQLAlchemy ORM examples
- [Cookbook — Async](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/fundamentals/async): pycubrid.aio and the SQLAlchemy async engine
- [Cookbook — Alembic](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/fundamentals/alembic): Programmatic Alembic migrations with sqlalchemy-cubrid
- [Cookbook — FastAPI service](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python/tree/main/templates/api-service-fastapi): REST API template with FastAPI and SQLAlchemy

## Ecosystem

- [pycubrid](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/pycubrid): Pure-Python DB-API 2.0 driver for CUBRID (recommended driver)
- [cubrid-cookbook-python](https://github.com/cubrid-lab/cubrid-cookbook-python): Runnable Python examples for CUBRID
- [CUBRID](https://www.cubrid.org/): The CUBRID database
